stored_text.note: official.html is the El Peruano HTML edition of DS 115-2025-PCM with the full Regulation (Titles I-VI, Articles 1-36, six final provisions). Article 24.1 jumps from item b) to item e) in the stored HTML: items c) and d) of the high-risk list are missing from the stored copy itself, not only from the text extraction. The Congress-hosted PDF that the verification note mentions is not stored.

english_version.note: No English text in the stored file. One web search found only English news (Andina, the state news agency) and law-firm summaries (DLA Piper, Morrison Foerster), no translation of the decree or the Regulation.

title.source_quote: Decreto Supremo que aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley Nº 31814, Ley que promueve el uso de la inteligencia artificial en favor del desarrollo económico y social del país
title.why: original_title is the stored heading with the number 'N° 115-2025-PCM' inserted (the stored text prints it separately as 'DECRETO SUPREMO nº 115-2025-pcm') and with '°' where the heading has 'º'. The English title renders the heading correctly but stops after 'artificial intelligence', leaving out 'for the economic and social development of the country'; that is a shortening, not a mistranslation.

summary_claims.claim: Prohibits ... lethal autonomous capability without human oversight.
summary_claims.original_quote: b) Generar capacidad letal autónoma, que comprenda la toma de decisiones sin supervisión humana y que pueda generar daño físico o afectar la vida y la integridad de las personas o grupos poblacionales en el ámbito civil.
summary_claims.literal_translation: b) Generating autonomous lethal capability that involves decision-making without human supervision and that may cause physical harm or affect the life and integrity of persons or population groups in the civilian sphere.

summary_claims.claim: Prohibits real-time public biometric identification (narrow exceptions).
summary_claims.original_quote: e) Realizar identificación biométrica en tiempo real para la categorización de personas naturales en espacios públicos. Salvo en los siguientes escenarios: i) Realizar una verificación biométrica que tenga como fin único la autenticación de la identidad digital; y, ii) Realizar investigación
summary_claims.literal_translation: e) Carrying out real-time biometric identification for the categorisation of natural persons in public spaces. Except in the following scenarios: i) carrying out biometric verification whose sole purpose is authentication of digital identity; and ii) carrying out the [preliminary] investigation [of a list of serious offences]

summary_claims.locator: Reglamento, Artículo 28.2 (Título VI, Capítulo I, obligations of public administration entities)
summary_claims.original_quote: 28.2 Para el desarrollo de sistemas basados en IA, deben usar la NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025 Tecnología de la información. Inteligencia artificial. Sistema de gestión (SGIA).
summary_claims.literal_translation: 28.2 For the development of AI-based systems, they [public administration entities] must use NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025 Information technology. Artificial intelligence. Management system (AIMS).

key_terms.note: Literally 'improper use'; Article 22.1(a) says such use 'deviene en prohibido' (becomes prohibited). The register describes the effect, not the category name; a reader searching for the Peruvian term would want 'improper use (prohibited)'.
Literal. Article 22.2 adds a residual 'riesgo aceptable' (acceptable risk) tier that the summary does not name.

key_terms.original: capacidad letal autónoma ... en el ámbito civil
key_terms.register_rendering: lethal autonomous capability without human oversight
key_terms.note: The rendering of the term is literal, but the qualifier 'en el ámbito civil' (in the civilian sphere) is dropped, and Article 4(b) excludes AI used for national defence and security from the Regulation's scope (subject to principles). Without the qualifier the summary reads as a general ban on lethal autonomous systems.

issues: The ban on autonomous lethal capability (Art. 23.1(b)) is limited to the civilian sphere, and defence and national-security uses are outside the Regulation's scope (Art. 4(b)); the summary leaves out both points, and the topic tag 'national security & military' adds to the impression of military coverage.

'narrow exceptions' to the real-time biometric identification ban is an evaluation: the exceptions cover digital-identity authentication and the preliminary investigation of a long list of serious offences (crimes against life, liberty, property and public administration, money laundering, drug trafficking, illegal mining, sexual offences, organised crime). The ban also concerns identification 'for the categorisation of natural persons'.

Security audits and incident management (Art. 29(c)-(d)) are duties of public administration entities for any AI system they develop or use, not obligations attached to high-risk uses in general, as the summary's sentence suggests.
The English title is shortened: it leaves out 'for the economic and social development of the country'.
The stored El Peruano HTML lacks items c) and d) of Article 24.1 (high-risk uses); the register's list of high-risk uses could not be checked against them.
note: The other prohibited uses (manipulation, unlawful mass surveillance, inference of sensitive data from biometrics, crime prediction by profiling) and the high-risk list (critical national assets, evaluation of minors in education, employment, social programmes, credit scoring except fraud detection, health) match Articles 23.1 and 24.1. The phased deadlines in notes match the First Final Complementary Provision, and the mandatory/voluntary split of impact assessments matches Articles 30.1 and 32.1.
